title: Token fingerprinting harness for per-model throughput + p95 regression detection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create and maintain a reproducible microbenchmark harness that fingerprints tokens/sec and p95 latency for our core served model variants (float32, int8/quantized, and compiled-kernel builds). This harness will be the canonical source-of-truth for per-model throughput baselines used by CI, rollout decisions, and billing guidance. It must exercise streaming & non-streaming paths, warm KV cache behavior, and sequence-length sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can run against any model in the catalog with a single CLI invocation and emit JSON artifacts (median tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99 latencies, and raw token timelines) to s3://redwood-benchmarks/eng/ENG-35789/<date>/.
acceptance_criteria_2: 2) Benchmarks include three canonical sequences (short=64, mid=256, long=1024) and two traffic modes: single-request throughput and steady-streaming concurrency; each target reports median and p95.
acceptance_criteria_3: 3) CI integration: a regression detector job consumes the artifact and flags PRs when median throughput drops >7% vs baseline OR p95 latency increases >15% OR statistical test (Wilcoxon) yields p<0.01 for user-impactful distributions.
acceptance_criteria_4: 4) Results visible in Console per-model dashboard and hooked into alerting channel (slack #runtime-bench-regressions) with actionable links to raw artifacts and diffs.
implementation_notes: - Language: harness in Python for quick iteration; critical runner components in Go micro-binary for parallel load generation.
implementation_notes_2: - Use runtime gRPC endpoint when available for lower client overhead; fallback to REST path for parity tests.
implementation_notes_3: - Warmup protocol: 3x warmup runs with same prompt length to populate KV cache; separate cold-run mode for cache-less baselines.
implementation_notes_4: - Sampling: capture per-token timestamps at 1ms resolution; compress timeline to newline-delimited JSON and upload.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for result parsing & baseline diff logic. 2) End-to-end nightly job that runs on the smallest Dedicated pool (dev-dedicated-smoke) and writes artifacts. 3) Canary: run harness on every runtime-1.22 canary build and compare to last successful baseline. 4) Statistical validation harness that generates synthetic noise to ensure false-positive rate <1%.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike prototype completed — basic single-request runner implemented and validated against local docker runtime.
2026-03-04: Integrated per-token timestamping and S3 artifact upload; created first artifact set for model 'open-7b' quantized-int8.
2026-03-06: Observed large variance on p95 for streaming workloads when batch size autoscaling is enabled; opened follow-up ENG-35802 to stabilize autoscaler interaction.
2026-03-09: Regression detector design doc posted; threshold defaults proposed (7% median, 15% p95). Planning CI gating after one-week of nightly runs.
2026-03-10: Initial Console integration POC implemented; webhook posts summary card to #runtime-bench-regressions.
notes: Design decision: we will treat median tokens/sec as primary SLO metric for throughput regressions and p95 as the safety metric for tail latency. For models with known cold-start penalties (large kv) we store both cold and warm baselines.
risks_mitigations: Risk: noisy artifacts from multi-tenant infra. Mitigation: run nightly on isolated dev-dedicated pool and annotate artifacts with instance topology. Risk: false positives in PR gating. Mitigation: use two-stage gate — warn on first failure and block only on persistent regressions across 3 runs.
next_steps: 1) Finish Go runner shim and add retries/backoff, 2) Add baseline management service to mark canonical baselines and roll forward, 3) Wire regression detector to PR checks and implement auto-muted exceptions for experimental models.
